text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government will stick to its practice of using authorised commercial banks to work with state budget funds alongside with a state Treasury, according to a decree signed by President Boris Yeltsin.
- Machine-building giant Uralmash, which became holding company Uralmash-Zavody last year, will issue new shares in June or July this year.

- The President of Tatarstan, one of the biggest republics on the territory of Russia, said on Tuesday that the republic will reconsider its relations with Russia if the latter signs a union treaty with Belarus.
- The government is expected to auction its shares in some Russian oil companies during the current year.
- One of the plants of industial holding Rosprom announced on Tuesday a deal worth $5.8 million on pipeline sections to be supplied to a state Iranian company.
- Three big commercial banks have agreed to finance the building of new boats for Russi's fishing fleet.
- Dagestan, a Caucasian republic boadering Chechnya, is on the edge of religious war, says the paper in connection with bloody clashes reported from the region on Tuesday.
- Russia and USA are holding talks on the possibility of using the Alpha Interanational Space Station for military purposes, says the paper.

- The law on asserting Russian ownership of art works seized from Nazi Germany during the World War Two, will not work even if parliament overrules the president's veto, says the president's representative in Federation Council, which is due to announce its position on Wednesday.
- The time for idle debate has expired, says the paper in connection with talks held in Moscow between Russia and NATO.

- Russian ministry of education has started sex education in secondary shools but the conservative parliamentary committee threatens education officials with responsibility for revealing intimate details of sex relations.

- Driven to despair by financial problems a 47-year-old mother comitted suicide after killing her six-year-old daughter. Such a wild way of solving problems is becoming more popular in Moscow, says the paper.
- Food prices rose 7.1 percent in Moscow in the last four months.
